title: Nonconvex–strongly concave minimax: Moreau stationarity with zero-respecting fresh gradients
summary: Minimize the worst-case joint-gradient call cap for expected Moreau-envelope stationarity under a public dual box and a primal–dual initialization-gap budget.

assumptions.description: The full gradient is $L$-Lipschitz in the product Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathcal Y$.
For each fixed $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu$-strongly concave on the public box $\mathcal Y$.
Neither $x\mapsto f(x,y)$ nor the optimal-value function $\Phi$ is additionally assumed convex.

assumptions.scope: Public initial point; the objective-gap or distance term refers to the same solution or value function explicitly specified in this entry

assumptions.description: $f$ is $C^2$ on an open neighborhood of the query domain.

model.parameter_domain_description: $d_x,d_y\ge1$, $G,L,\varepsilon>0$, $0<\mu\le L$, $\sigma\ge0$, and $\kappa=L/\mu$. The dual box may have any finite radii.
description_paragraphs: Let $\mathcal Y$ be a public bounded coordinate box containing the origin. The start is $(x_0,y_0)=(0,0)$. The unknown payoff $f$ is $C^2$ on a neighborhood of $\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathcal Y$ and jointly $L$-smooth on this domain in the Euclidean norm.
For every $x$, the function $f(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu$-strongly concave on $\mathcal Y$. For every $y\in\mathcal Y$, the function $f(\cdot,y)$ is bounded below. There is no primal convexity assumption.
The public budget $G$ bounds the initial primal–dual gap. This is the gap between the best dual value at the initial primal point and the smallest primal value at the initial dual point.

operations.order_convention: Derivative order refers to the scalar payoff $f$. The joint gradient has two blocks; the response signature specifies whether a Hessian or complete derivative jet is supplied.

feedback_quality.description: The explicit inequalities specify conditional means, joint variance, and whether paired-sample reuse is allowed.

operations.coupling: Each call uses a fresh sample. The same random sample cannot be reused at a second point, and mean-square Lipschitz regularity of stochastic gradients is not implicit.

public_inputs: Public inputs are the block dimensions $d_x,d_y$, the box endpoints, $L,\mu,G,\sigma,\varepsilon$, and the origin start.
auxiliary_interfaces: Coordinatewise Euclidean projection onto the public box is computed directly from its endpoints.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs are the block dimensions $d_x,d_y$, the box endpoints, $L,\mu,G,\sigma,\varepsilon$, and the origin start.

At an adaptively chosen feasible point $(x,y)$, receive one fresh full vector $G_f(x,y;\xi)=(G_x,G_y)$. Conditional on the previous transcript and the current query, its mean is $\nabla f(x,y)$ and its expected squared Euclidean error is at most $\sigma^2$.

The two blocks may be dependent within the response. The sample is independent of earlier samples and cannot be reused at a second query point. The oracle response need not be the gradient of a scalar sample loss.
Projection onto $\mathcal Y$ uses the public box endpoints. The payoff, inner maximizers, and the Moreau gradient are hidden.

output.feasibility: Return $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^{d_x}$ with the support condition in ALGORITHMS.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable primal output obeying the previously revealed support. A query at the output point is optional.
description_paragraphs: Return a single primal vector $\widehat x$. Every nonzero coordinate of $\widehat x$ must have appeared in a primal response. A dual vector or a certificate is unnecessary.

metric.normalization: Unsquared Euclidean norm evaluated at the returned point.
metric.finiteness_conditions: $\Phi$ is finite and $L$-weakly convex, so $\eta=1/(2L)$ gives a unique proximal point and a finite envelope gradient.
description_paragraphs: Set $\eta=1/(2L)$ and define the Moreau envelope of the primal value by
Evaluate the unsquared norm $\|\nabla\Phi_{\eta}(\widehat x)\|_2$. The proximal point in this definition is part of the evaluation criterion.

components.description: Number of full joint-gradient queries using fresh samples

resource.scalarization: only the explicitly selected query component is optimized; all auxiliary costs retained
resource.precision_model: exact real responses; arithmetic and bit costs uncharged; no finite-bit conclusion
description_paragraphs: One full joint-gradient sample costs one $N_{\rm grad}$ call. Both blocks are returned together and do not count as two calls.
Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

algorithms.adaptivity: Sequential adaptive queries and outputs within the stated blockwise support constraints.
algorithms.internal_computation: exact real arithmetic and arbitrary measurable transcript-based internal computation uncharged; no bound on arithmetic or bits is inferred
algorithms.parallelism: sequential; parallel rounds not identified with calls
description_paragraphs: The first query is at the origin and the zero-query output is zero. Each later primal and dual query block is supported on the union of coordinates observed in its own response block. The output is supported on the observed primal union.
The algorithm can adapt to all past responses and use private randomness independent of the samples. Discovered coordinates can return to zero. The restriction uses the union over the full history.

aggregation_order: For every fixed instance, take expectation of the unsquared Euclidean norm over the stated randomness.
guarantees.quantifier_order: choose a single algorithm from public inputs, then all compatible hidden instances and legal oracle rules
randomness_sources: Private random seed of the algorithm
Fresh-sample stochastic response specified in this profile
guarantees.time_uniformity: fixed target accuracy; not an anytime guarantee
description_paragraphs: For each fixed feasible instance and oracle law, $\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi_\eta(\widehat x)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. The expectation is over the algorithm's private randomness and the fresh oracle samples.

budget.precision_model: exact real responses; arithmetic and bit costs uncharged; no finite-bit conclusion
budget.scalarization: only the explicitly selected query component is optimized; all auxiliary costs retained

objects.definition: Unknown scalar payoff $f$ defined on an open neighborhood of $\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathcal Y$.
$\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathcal Y}f(x,y)$ with a unique dual maximizer. Its Moreau envelope is defined in METRIC.

domains.definition: Public product $\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathcal Y$ with $\mathcal Y$ a bounded box containing zero.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$.

bracket.envelope_certificate: Upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants under Zhou's Theorem 1.
The quotient is at most a universal multiple of $\kappa/(1+\kappa\sigma^2/\varepsilon^2)$. The stated bounds do not determine the optimum throughout this window.
The SAPD+ upper bound is available here. No matching lower bound is certified by the cited construction.
